evidence.note: Recon phase is sequenced (routes -> migrations -> models -> specs -> db -> middleware), showing some ordering instinct, but the 'Plan' fields are next-action plans ('read X, then generate Rust'), not an explicit milestone breakdown with completion criteria.

Implementation written as a single monolithic main.rs covering schemas, sessions, posts, comments, follows, notifications, feeds, media, and admin all at once — a bundled push rather than ordered, independently-verifiable subsystem milestones each with a done-check.
Smoke test hits health/register/post/comment/feed/admin as a rough done-signal, but applied to the whole system after the fact rather than per-milestone as it was built.

Recognizes shared-DB schema parity and header parity as risks only reactively after implementing — a real de-risking insight, but not sequenced as a foundational early milestone; parity issues are patched as discovered.

reasoning: The agent held a mental list of subsystems and sequenced its recon and post-hoc smoke tests sensibly, which lifts it above a pure anchor-3 'vague mental list.' But it never produced an explicit ordered milestone plan with per-subsystem done-checks; instead it wrote one monolithic implementation and verified/patched reactively, so it falls short of anchor 5's explicit subsystem breakdown with a rough done-signal per piece. This places observed behavior at 4 — between the vague-list and explicit-breakdown anchors, with a genuine but late shared-schema de-risking realization keeping it from dropping to 3.
